question: Under the HIV Act 2017, a doctor who refuses to perform surgery on a patient solely because the patient is HIV-positive commits a violation that is punishable under the Act.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is true. The HIV Act 2017 prohibits discrimination in healthcare, including refusal of treatment. A surgeon who refuses to operate on an HIV-positive patient without other clinical justification violates the Act.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. The HIV Act 2017 contains explicit anti-discrimination provisions. Refusing to treat a person solely on the basis of their HIV status is discrimination under the Act and attracts penalties. Healthcare workers are specifically prohibited from refusing treatment on this ground.
